nodes.rationale: Protocol is symmetric so same-platform pairs work later, but only cross-platform is tested in v1; iOS forbids background receiving; different networks need a relay.

nodes.label: Principle: Receiver Is the Server
nodes.rationale: The receiving phone runs the HTTPS server and the sender is the client so the model works the same in every network mode.

nodes.label: Principle: One Shared Dart Core
nodes.rationale: Protocol, engine, security and UI are shared Dart; native Swift/Kotlin only where the OS requires it (photo library, hotspot, background, Bonjour).

nodes.label: Principle: Never Trust the Network
nodes.rationale: TLS 1.3 pinned to the receiver, sender proves its key, receiver approves unknown senders.

nodes.label: Principle: Fail Loudly and Suggest the Next Mode
Platform Channels (paths and file descriptors only)
nodes.rationale: File bytes never cross platform channels; Dart reads files directly to avoid copies and memory pressure.

nodes.label: Connectivity Scenarios (10-row table)
nodes.rationale: Hotspot modes usually fastest because data crosses the air once instead of twice via a router; must be benchmarked before claiming.

nodes.label: Android LocalOnlyHotspot Mode (D-054, D-055)
nodes.rationale: Recommended offline mode; one QR carries Wi-Fi credentials plus connection info; iPhone joins via NEHotspotConfiguration only with paid Apple account capability, otherwise guided through Settings.

nodes.label: iPhone Personal Hotspot Guide (D-057)
nodes.rationale: Apps cannot turn on Personal Hotspot, so a three-step guide with live checks is used.

nodes.label: Android Network Binding (bindProcessToNetwork, D-056)
nodes.rationale: Whole process is bound because dart:io creates its own sockets; applied when Wi-Fi is connected, not validated and not default.

nodes.label: Connection Flow (Wi-Fi -> QR -> Hotspot)
nodes.rationale: Tries the easiest mode first; every path ends in the same pinned authenticated TLS session so the engine never cares how phones connect.

nodes.label: Bonjour/mDNS Advertisement _crossdrop._tcp
nodes.rationale: Instance name CrossDrop-<8 chars of UUID> carries no personal data; advertises while app open and Receiving on (D-046), stops 30 s after hidden.

nodes.label: TXT Record (v, id, n, p, fp)
nodes.rationale: fp is a 16-hex hint only; full fingerprint checked in TLS. Records without a local-range IPv4 are ignored so an advertisement can never point outside the LAN.

nodes.label: QR Code Payload crossdrop://connect
nodes.rationale: Strict parsing: every parameter exactly once, unknown ignored for forward compatibility, local IPv4 only, never resolved, never logged; hotspot variant adds ws/wp/wsec.

nodes.label: WebSocket Events (accepted, rejected, progress, file_done, cancelled, error)
nodes.rationale: Events are a convenience; every fact is also in HTTP replies so a lost socket never stops a transfer.

nodes.label: Offer Limits (10,000 files, 1 TiB/file, 4 TiB total, 8 sessions)
nodes.rationale: Caps chosen so no sum of sizes can overflow (review H2); D-023, D-032.

nodes.label: Offer Manifest JSON
nodes.rationale: SHA-256 is not in the offer so sending can start before hashing finishes; sender id/name are labels only.

nodes.label: Free-Space Check (offer + open sessions + 64 MB reserve)
Checkpoint Every 2 s or 64 MB (D-022, D-065)
nodes.rationale: fsync then save the byte count; after a crash the file is cut back so about 2 s is resent; keeps fsyncs and DB writes low.

nodes.label: Receiver 8 MB Read-Ahead Write Queue (D-064)
nodes.rationale: Separate writer (write, hash, checkpoint) so disk work does not stall the connection.

nodes.label: Incremental SHA-256 Verification (D-021)
nodes.rationale: Computed while writing and kept across drops; rehashed from disk after app restart; mismatch restarts once then fails.

nodes.label: Device Identity (ECDSA P-256 self-signed cert, D-028, D-030)
nodes.rationale: Key in Keychain / Keystore-protected storage; cert subject CN=CrossDrop holds no personal data; reinstall gives a new identity.

nodes.label: Certificate SHA-256 Fingerprint as Identity
nodes.rationale: Device name and UUID can be faked, so no decision is ever based on them.

nodes.label: dart:io TLS Capability Findings (D-027)
nodes.rationale: dart:io has no server-side callback to accept unknown self-signed client certificates, so mutual TLS is replaced with application-layer sender authentication; header limit fixed at 1 MB so own 16 KB middleware is used.

nodes.label: Application-Layer Sender Authentication (signed challenge)
nodes.rationale: Signature covers the receiver fingerprint so a proof is useless at another receiver and cannot be relayed; token only inside pinned TLS.

nodes.label: Sender Commitment crossdrop-commit-v2 (D-061)
nodes.rationale: Sender commits to its certificate and nonce before seeing the receiver nonce, so a MITM gets one chance in a million instead of grinding keys or certificates.

nodes.label: Bearer Token (32 bytes, 1 h idle expiry)
Where the Receiver's Fingerprint Comes From (QR, trusted, probeFingerprint)
6-Digit Pairing Code crossdrop-code-v1 (D-029)
nodes.rationale: Like Bluetooth numeric comparison; derived from both fingerprints and both nonces; a fingerprint-only code could be forced by a MITM in about a million tries. Known answer 828838.

nodes.label: Per-IP Rate Limits and Request Limits (D-031, D-032)
Memory and Database Hygiene (review M1, M2, L3)
Server Lifetime (D-046, D-050, D-062, review M6)
nodes.rationale: Runs only while app open and switch on; new random port each start; iOS may reclaim the socket while suspended (TN2277), so a loopback connect check restarts it on return.

nodes.label: File Name Sanitization (review L8)
nodes.rationale: Strip paths, control, bidi and zero-width characters and reserved names; sanitized on arrival so every screen shows the saved name.

nodes.label: Privacy (no accounts, no analytics, 8-char fingerprint logs)
iOS Local Network Permission Bonjour Self-Probe (D-015)
Android fd Streaming via pread / dart:ffi (D-036)
nodes.rationale: Kotlin hands over only the descriptor number; Dart reads it in a background isolate without copying.

nodes.label: MediaStore Pending Item as Partial File (D-040)
nodes.rationale: Pending item is the partial file and is published once verified: no extra copy, no permission.

nodes.label: HEIC/Live Photo Format Settings (D-039)
nodes.rationale: Default sends originals (HEIC, still only); JPEG conversion at 0.92 and Live Photo MOV are opt-in settings.

nodes.label: iOS Share Extension App Group Inbox (D-045)
Cable Import iPhone -> Android (D-067)
nodes.rationale: Not the HTTPS protocol: Android is USB host reading the iPhone PTP camera interface; iPhone needs no app; PTP has no hash so only exact size is checked; iOS exposes only the camera roll.

Failure Handling Table
nodes.rationale: Every failure ends in automatic resume, a clear message with the next step, or a clean cancel with no half-saved files.

nodes.rationale: Custom protocol chosen for v1; LocalSend compatibility may be considered after v1; used as a speed comparison.

nodes.label: Decisions log (DECISIONS.md)
nodes.rationale: Append-only log of hard-to-reverse design decisions; superseded entries are marked, never rewritten.

nodes.label: D-001: Receiver runs the HTTPS server
nodes.rationale: One code path for every network mode (hotspot/router, iOS cannot host a hotspot); both phones must run a server, only while the app is open.

nodes.label: D-002: Plain HTTPS with streamed PUT for file bytes
nodes.rationale: Gigabyte files must be resumable without loading into memory; works with dart:io/shelf, testable without phones; resume = GET + PUT ?offset=N.

nodes.label: D-003: Mutual TLS with pinned self-signed certificates
nodes.rationale: No account or CA to vouch for identity; the certificate SHA-256 fingerprint is the identity. Superseded in part by D-027.

nodes.label: D-004: Flutter, native code only where the OS requires it
nodes.rationale: Shared Dart for protocol/engine/security/UI keeps most code testable on a PC; channels carry paths or fds, never bytes.

nodes.label: D-005: No cloud server in v1
nodes.rationale: A relay adds cost, accounts and privacy exposure; nothing leaves the local network. WebRTC+TURN is a possible future addition.

nodes.label: D-006: shelf and shelf_router for the receive server
nodes.rationale: Dart-team packages; Request.read() streams bodies; handlers testable over loopback.

nodes.label: D-007: crypto package for SHA-256 instead of cryptography
nodes.rationale: sha256.startChunkedConversion is synchronous pure Dart and fits a chunk-by-chunk isolate loop.

nodes.label: D-008: basic_utils to create the self-signed certificate
nodes.rationale: dart:io cannot create certificates; basic_utils (pointycastle) is pure Dart, ~170 ms generation, accepted by dart:io HTTPS.

nodes.label: D-009: file_picker for picking files in Phase 1
nodes.rationale: PoC needs any-file picking without native code; copies to cache, later replaced by fd streaming and PhotoKit export.

nodes.label: D-010: Supporting packages for Phase 1
nodes.rationale: flutter_riverpod, path_provider, wakelock_plus (iOS pauses on lock), path.

nodes.label: D-011: Phase 1 client accepts any server certificate; offers auto-accepted
nodes.rationale: PoC had no fingerprint to pin; acceptable only for dev builds. Superseded by D-027 and D-033.

nodes.label: D-012: bonsoir for Bonjour/mDNS discovery
nodes.rationale: Uses NWBrowser/DNSServiceRegister on iOS and NsdManager on Android with ref-counted multicast lock; no raw multicast entitlement; behind MdnsBackend for fakes.

nodes.label: D-013: drift for the local database
nodes.rationale: Typed tables and migrations via schemaVersion; NativeDatabase.memory() tests on PC; generated database.g.dart committed.

nodes.label: D-014: Packages for QR codes and network changes
nodes.rationale: qr_flutter, mobile_scanner, connectivity_plus plus 3 s NetworkInterface polling; avoided network_info_plus (location permission), uuid, app_settings, device_info_plus.

nodes.label: D-015: Detect iOS Local Network denial with a Bonjour self-probe
nodes.rationale: iOS has no API to read Local Network permission and bonsoir ignores PolicyDenied; a Swift NWListener/NWBrowser self-probe yields granted/denied/unknown.

nodes.label: D-016: Phase 2 advertises only while Receive is open, per-launch fingerprint
nodes.rationale: Auto-accept made always-on advertising unsafe; TXT/QR fp formats final early. Superseded in part by D-028, D-031 and D-046.

nodes.label: D-017: GitHub Actions builds; iPhone sideloaded with a free Apple ID
nodes.rationale: No Mac available; unsigned IPA via macOS runner, installed with Sideloadly; 7-day expiry; paid capabilities unavailable; macOS minutes cost 10x so builds are manual.

nodes.label: D-018: Sessions start as offered; status endpoint and event replay
nodes.rationale: A late or reconnecting event socket would miss the Accept answer; GET /v1/sessions/{id}, replay on connect, 2 s polling.

nodes.label: D-019: Retry backoff 1, 2, 4, 8 s, then 8 s, for about 2 minutes
nodes.rationale: Capped backoff keeps resume within ~10 s; progress resets delay and deadline; re-lookup by device id after 3 failures.

nodes.label: D-020: Free space through a small platform channel
nodes.rationale: Dart has no free-space API; StatFs on Android, volumeAvailableCapacityForImportantUsage on iOS behind FreeSpace interface.

nodes.label: D-021: Resume without re-hashing what was already sent
nodes.rationale: Re-hashing a 2 GB prefix exceeds the 15 s stall timeout; sender hashes in parallel isolate, receiver keeps incremental hash across drops.

nodes.label: D-022: Checkpoint = fsync, then store receivedBytes; restore cuts back
nodes.rationale: A crashed part file may contain garbage past what reached disk; truncate to stored receivedBytes. Interval superseded by D-065.

nodes.label: D-023: Receiver limits and what too many bytes does
nodes.rationale: Oversized file fails just that file; one session per sender (409 sender_busy), 8 sessions max, 10,000 files, free-space + 64 MB margin.

nodes.label: D-024: Keep-alive with flutter_foreground_task and an iOS background task
nodes.rationale: Android needs a dataSync foreground service; iOS suspends hidden apps, so beginBackgroundTask saves progress and pauses.

nodes.label: D-025: Partial files in the app support folder
nodes.rationale: OS temp/cache may be purged while closed, breaking resume; 24-hour cleanup at launch.

nodes.label: D-026: Multi-gigabyte tests are tagged and skipped by default
nodes.rationale: 2 GB test needs ~4 GB disk and minutes; tagged large, run before calling a phase done.

nodes.label: D-027: Sender authentication by signed challenge
nodes.rationale: dart:io (BoringSSL) drops self-signed client certs it does not already trust and has no server-side callback; sender pins receiver and proves its key with an ECDSA-signed nonce challenge for a bearer token.

nodes.label: D-028: basic_utils for the persistent device identity
nodes.rationale: Persistent P-256 key and 20-year self-signed cert; deterministic RFC 6979 signing; no new package. Pitfall: ecSign/ecVerify default to SHA-1.

nodes.label: D-029: Pairing code includes committed nonces, not only fingerprints
nodes.rationale: A MITM could grind keys to match a fingerprint-only code in ~10^6 tries; nonces with sender commit-first as in Bluetooth numeric comparison.

nodes.label: D-030: flutter_secure_storage for the private key; app backup off
nodes.rationale: Key must live in Keychain/Keystore and never migrate to another phone; identity row in DB is the source of truth.

nodes.label: D-031: The Receiving switch and server lifetime
nodes.rationale: Global on/off switch: off rejects untrusted offers with 403 receiving_off and drains the server without breaking running transfers.

nodes.label: D-032: Abuse limits
nodes.rationale: Per-IP token buckets for offers and auth, header/body size caps, memory caps and idle timeouts since anyone on the Wi-Fi can reach the server.

nodes.label: D-033: First contact, lookalikes and trust records
nodes.rationale: Without QR, probeFingerprint over one TLS handshake, checked against TXT hint; trust by fingerprint only; lookalike warning for same name/id with other key.

nodes.label: D-034: Database lives in Application Support, not Documents
nodes.rationale: iOS Documents is visible in Files (UIFileSharingEnabled) and holds received files; one-time migration at startup.

nodes.label: D-035: Android minimum SDK 29 (Android 10)
nodes.rationale: MediaStore IS_PENDING, RELATIVE_PATH and Downloads collection need API 29; avoids a second save path with WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE.

nodes.label: D-036: Android files read/written through file descriptors with dart:ffi
nodes.rationale: Content URIs cannot be wrapped by dart:io and /proc/self/fd reopen is refused; Kotlin detaches fd, Dart uses pread/pwrite via FFI in FdWorker isolate.

nodes.label: D-037: Read Android originals with setRequireOriginal and ACCESS_MEDIA_LOCATION
nodes.rationale: MediaStore strips GPS otherwise, changing file and hash; falls back to redacted file with original:false.

nodes.label: D-038: Prepare picked items before the offer; own iOS exporter
nodes.rationale: Offer needs exact sizes; iOS assets may be in iCloud or converted; photo_manager originFile lacks cancel/stall detection, so PHAssetResourceManager export to staging.

nodes.label: D-039: HEIC, Live Photo and video format rules
nodes.rationale: Default to originals (HEIC, Live Photo still only); optional HEIC->JPEG and Live Photo MOV settings for non-iPhone receivers; no transcoding.

nodes.label: D-040: Android receives straight into a pending MediaStore item
nodes.rationale: Writing to .part then copying needs double space; ReceivedFileStore interface, collection chosen from sanitized extension, publish when verified.

nodes.label: D-041: Document pickers: SAF in place on Android, a copy on iOS
nodes.rationale: file_picker copies on Android; own ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT with persistable grants. iOS security-scoped URL lifetimes too fragile, so import-mode copy.

nodes.label: D-042: Creation dates
nodes.rationale: Keep creation date where the platform allows: PHAssetCreationRequest.creationDate, DATE_TAKEN, futimens; documented platform limits.

nodes.label: D-043: iOS saving: Photos with add-only access, moved; Files fallback
nodes.rationale: shouldMoveFile avoids a copy and add-only needs no read access; unsupported formats or denial go to Documents.

nodes.label: D-044: Android share target: SEND and SEND_MULTIPLE, singleTask
nodes.rationale: singleTop would spawn a second engine/DB/server; only content:// URIs from other apps accepted to avoid leaking private files.

nodes.label: D-045: iOS Share Extension hands files via an App Group inbox
nodes.rationale: Share extensions have ~120 MB memory limit and must not transfer; extension clones files to group inbox, writes manifest.json, opens crossdrop://share.

nodes.label: D-046: Home is the receive screen; receiving runs while the app is open
nodes.rationale: Phase 6 Home shows Ready to receive; ReceiveHost above navigator; server stops after 30 s hidden and idle. Changes D-016 and D-031.

nodes.label: D-047: Navigation with Navigator and named routes
nodes.rationale: go_router would add a dependency for ~12 screens and no deep links.

nodes.label: D-048: One transfer view model for both directions
nodes.rationale: TransferView built from SendSnapshot or IncomingSession so Progress/Done/Failed/History screens are shared and testable.

nodes.label: D-049: Failure messages come from one table
nodes.rationale: failure_messages.dart maps reason codes to title, reason, next step and one button; pin mismatch never offers retry.

nodes.label: D-050: Onboarding first; receiving starts after it
nodes.rationale: Avoid the iOS Local Network prompt appearing before it is explained; settings.onboardingDone schema 5.

nodes.label: D-051: Open received files through own channel
nodes.rationale: open_filex handles paths only; crossdrop/open channel uses ACTION_VIEW for MediaStore URIs and photos-redirect:// or Quick Look on iOS.

nodes.label: D-052: Send picks files first, then the phone
nodes.rationale: Matches the brief's Send screen and share-sheet entry with files preselected; totals say at least until prepared.

nodes.label: D-053: The sender can pause
nodes.rationale: Reuses engine pause from iOS backgrounding; user pause remembered; receiver has no pause (Cancel covers it).

nodes.label: D-054: Android hotspot: LocalOnlyHotspot, owned by its screen
nodes.rationale: startLocalOnlyHotspot gives random credentials without internet; address found by diffing interface lists; QR gains ws/wp/wsec plus WIFI: code.

nodes.label: D-055: iPhone joins with NEHotspotConfiguration when possible, Settings otherwise
nodes.rationale: Hotspot Configuration capability needs a paid account (free CI builds lack it); embedded provisioning profile checked; Settings join with Copy password fallback.

nodes.label: D-056: Android binds the whole process to a Wi-Fi without internet
nodes.rationale: dart:io creates its own sockets so Network.getSocketFactory cannot be used; bindProcessToNetwork when Wi-Fi is unvalidated and not default.

nodes.label: D-057: Personal Hotspot guide checks prefixes, not names
nodes.rationale: Reading Wi-Fi name needs location/capabilities; subnet comparison (172.20.10.0/28 hints) needs no permission.

nodes.label: D-058: Benchmark builds: release-mode flag, benchmark files discarded
nodes.rationale: Debug numbers are useless; CROSSDROP_BENCH const flag on release builds; bench store deletes verified crossdrop-bench files; no protocol change.

nodes.label: D-059: One stream per transfer until benchmarks show a clear gain
nodes.rationale: Parallel streams complicate resume, hashing and receiver; considered only if single stream is well below link capacity without CPU limit.

nodes.label: D-060: No LocalSend compatibility in v1
nodes.rationale: Custom protocol with pinning, signed challenge, resume and 6-digit code already built and tested; revisit after v1 as an adapter.

nodes.label: D-061: Auth commitment covers both fingerprints; protocol version 2
nodes.rationale: Code review H1: v1 commitment fixed only the sender nonce, letting a MITM grind certificate variants in under a second; v2 commit binds receiverFp and senderFp; v1 unsupported.

nodes.label: D-062: Paused received session holds keep-alive and server for 150 s
nodes.rationale: Review M3/L6: holding forever drained resources, releasing immediately let iPhone lock during a brief Wi-Fi drop; 150 s = D-019 retry deadline plus margin; SessionKeepAlive class.

nodes.label: D-063: App id under owner's GitHub namespace; no debug-signed release; all rights reserved
nodes.rationale: Release blockers from review: io.github.shreyashjunje.crossdrop, release key required, LICENSE all rights reserved to keep options open.

nodes.label: D-064: Receiver reads ahead of the disk, up to 8 MB
nodes.rationale: Serial receive loop paused the body stream during writes/fsync so disk and network never overlapped; queue with 8 MB high / 4 MB low watermarks.

nodes.label: D-065: Checkpoint every 2 s or 64 MB, not every 4 MB
nodes.rationale: Frequent fsync + SQLite writes are costly on phone flash and Android FUSE; mechanism of D-022 unchanged.

nodes.label: D-066: Measure each phone's limits first; bigger speed changes wait for numbers
nodes.rationale: No TLS-off/hash-off modes (downgrade risk, hard rule 4); Measure this phone times SHA-256, TLS loopback and store writes; native SHA-256, overlapping files, streaming export, Wi-Fi Direct gated on numbers.

nodes.label: D-067: Import from an iPhone by cable through its camera interface (PTP) on Android
nodes.rationale: Public android.mtp.MtpDevice API works with USB-C and Lightning iPhones without an iPhone app; usbmux is undocumented and fragile; iPhone->Android camera roll only, into pending MediaStore items, no hash available.

nodes.label: Smoke tests P6-3, P6-4, P4-1, P7-9
nodes.rationale: Four checks confirm the core works on real phones before running the full 90-check pass.

nodes.label: Network Setup Labels (Router 2.4/5 GHz, Android hotspot, iPhone hotspot)
Step 0: Measure This Phone (per-phone limits)
nodes.rationale: Isolates sha256, TLS loopback and fsync write costs without the radio so the ceiling of a transfer can be identified (step within 1.5x of transfer MB/s is the ceiling).

nodes.label: Step A: Choose the Buffer Size (256 KB / 1 MB / 4 MB)
nodes.rationale: Winner rule: median, sizes >= 100 MB, within 5% of best on every network and direction, ties go to 1 MB; default changes only in a separate commit with justifying numbers.

nodes.label: Fair LocalSend Comparison Protocol
nodes.rationale: Alternate apps run by run so heat and battery affect both; both use Android Settings tethering because LocalSend cannot use CrossDrop's in-app hotspot; LocalSend timed from receiver screen recording.

nodes.label: Parallel Streams (not built, D-059)
nodes.rationale: Proposed only if CrossDrop is more than ~25% below iperf3 while neither phone's CPU is near one core.

nodes.label: H1: Auth Commitment Covers Both Fingerprints (Protocol v2, D-061)
nodes.rationale: Prevents a man in the middle from choosing a certificate that makes both pairing codes match; version 1 refused.

nodes.label: H2: Declared Size Caps (1 TiB file, 4 TiB offer)
nodes.rationale: Stops sizes from wrapping the 64-bit total and slipping past the free-space check.

nodes.label: H4: iPhone Share vs Launch Cleanup
M6: iPhone Server Health Check and Restart After Lock
M4: Pause Kept Until Upload Sees It
M5/L4: Cancel While Connecting or Checking Address
L1: Exclusive File Creation to Claim Save Name
L5: Discard Old Resumable Send Properly
L7: Network Binding Changes Applied One at a Time
L8: Strip Bidi/Zero-width Chars from Names
nodes.rationale: photo<RLO>gpj.exe displayed as photoexe.jpg; receiver sanitizes on arrival so every screen shows the saved name.

nodes.label: Receiver 8 MB Socket Read-ahead (D-064)
nodes.rationale: Writing, hashing and checkpoints no longer stall the sender.

nodes.label: Sender Reads Next 1 MB While Sending
Android Descriptor I/O Native Buffer Reuse
Measure This Phone (D-066)
nodes.rationale: Each cost is known before the next speed change; larger speed items wait for the numbers.

nodes.label: Android Network Binding (D-056)
nodes.rationale: On Wi-Fi without internet, traffic stays on Wi-Fi instead of mobile data.

nodes.label: Onboarding (three pages)
nodes.rationale: Receiving, and so the iOS Local Network prompt, starts only after onboarding.

nodes.label: Receiving Runs Whenever App Is Open (D-046)
Media Picking (photo_manager gallery, SAF, document picker)
Format Handling (originals, HEIC to JPEG, D-042)
Share from Other Apps (iOS Share Extension, Android SEND)
Pairing and Trust (TLS 1.3 pinning, signed challenge)
Resume with Retry Backoff and 4 MB Checkpoints
Keep-alive (wakelock, foreground service, iOS background task)
Receiver Keeps Hash Across Drops (D-021)
nodes.rationale: Resuming a large file never re-reads what was sent.

nodes.label: CI Build Workflow (APK + unsigned IPA, D-017)
Feature doc structure (Summary, Scope, Design, Code, Protocol, Tests, Limits, Open questions)
nodes.rationale: Feature docs link to ARCHITECTURE.md sections instead of repeating them and record any deviation in DECISIONS.md.

nodes.label: Receiving switch (settings.receivingEnabled)
nodes.rationale: Anyone on the same Wi-Fi can reach the server while Receive is open; a global switch stops advertising, hides the QR and answers untrusted offers with 403 receiving_off.

nodes.label: RateLimiter (token bucket per remote IP)
nodes.rationale: Prevents a stranger flooding offers or auth; 1,024 tracked addresses with LRU eviction keeps memory bounded.

nodes.label: ServerLimits (header and body size limits)
nodes.rationale: dart:io only stops headers at 1 MB and cannot be configured, so the app enforces 16 KB headers and per-route body caps itself.

nodes.label: Session pruning (ReceiveServer.prune)
nodes.rationale: Review M1: ended sessions are forgotten and never-accepted offers deleted so a stranger cannot grow the database or History.

nodes.label: One hash isolate per session
nodes.rationale: Review M2.

nodes.label: Offer slots reserved before first await
nodes.rationale: Review L3: parallel offers from one sender get one session and 409 for the rest.

nodes.label: Order of checks for an offer (401, 429, 413, 400, 403, 409, 503, 507)
nodes.rationale: An unauthenticated flood never parses JSON, and a refused offer never reaches the Accept prompt.

nodes.label: Abuse error codes (403 receiving_off, 413 body_too_large, 429 rate_limited, 431 headers_too_large)
Server lifetime (random port, TLS 1.3 minimum, 30 s idle timeout)
LocalOnlyHotspot (WifiManager.startLocalOnlyHotspot)
nodes.rationale: No internet, no mobile data; used when there is no shared Wi-Fi or it isolates clients (scenario 4).

nodes.label: HotspotController
nodes.rationale: D-054: start, address wait, idle stop.

nodes.label: pickHotspotAddress
nodes.rationale: Prefers a new address on hotspot-like interfaces (swlan, ap, softap, wlan1+); mobile data and VPN never count.

nodes.label: QR Wi-Fi fields (ws, wp, wsec)
nodes.rationale: ws and wp come together or not at all; older apps ignore them.

nodes.label: Standard Wi-Fi QR for iPhone Camera (D-055)
nodes.rationale: For iPhone builds that cannot join from the app.

nodes.label: Hotspot error codes (permission, location_off, tethering_on, no_channel, ...)
Hotspot 60 s idle stop with Keep on
nodes.rationale: The hotspot belongs to the hotspot screen; it stops on leaving or 60 s after the last transfer (D-054, review H3 for cancel-while-starting).

nodes.label: shouldBindToWifi rule (D-056)
nodes.rationale: Bind only when Wi-Fi is connected, not validated and not default: Android otherwise routes new sockets over mobile data; a default VPN must keep routing (scenario 6).

nodes.label: ConnectivityManager.bindProcessToNetwork
nodes.rationale: Network.getSocketFactory() cannot reach sockets dart:io creates itself, so the whole process is bound; safe because CrossDrop makes no off-LAN calls (hard rule 8).

nodes.label: NetworkBinder
nodes.rationale: Applies changes one at a time, newest last (review L7).

nodes.label: CROSSDROP_BENCH build flag (D-058)
nodes.rationale: Release builds only: Flutter debug builds run Dart without full compilation, so their numbers mean nothing; const bool compiles the screen out of normal builds.

nodes.label: BenchRunner
nodes.rationale: Buffers alternate within each repeat so warm-up or neighbour traffic does not favour one buffer.

nodes.label: BenchDiscardingStore
nodes.rationale: Benchmark files are verified then deleted so 2 GB runs do not fill the gallery; no protocol change.

nodes.label: bestBuffer rule (median within 5 %)
nodes.rationale: 1 MB default wins a tie.

nodes.label: BenchResult CSV columns
nodes.rationale: No names, addresses or fingerprints (hard rule 7).

nodes.label: Phone limits measurement (D-066)
nodes.rationale: Measures SHA-256, TLS 1.3 loopback and write rates without the network; deliberately no TLS-off or hash-off mode (hard rule 4).

nodes.label: Parallel streams (D-059, not built)
nodes.rationale: Added only if measurements show a clear gain.

nodes.label: Process stats (CPU via getrusage, peak RSS)
DeviceCredentials (ECDSA P-256 key, self-signed cert)
nodes.rationale: Subject CN=CrossDrop only (no personal data), generated in an isolate.

nodes.label: CredentialRepository.loadOrCreate
nodes.rationale: Writes the key first, then the certificate, so a crash between leaves no matching pair; the identity row is the source of truth because iOS keeps Keychain items after uninstall.

nodes.label: Certificate SHA-256 fingerprint (device identity)
nodes.rationale: Pinning, trust, session ownership and the pairing code are all based on it.

nodes.label: SecretStore interface / MemorySecretStore
nodes.rationale: Hard rule 9.

nodes.label: credentialsProvider
nodes.rationale: Started from Home so the key exists before Receive or Send.

nodes.label: Software keys instead of hardware-backed keys (D-028)
nodes.rationale: Dart's TLS stack needs the private key as bytes.

nodes.label: TXT record (v, id, n, p, fp)
nodes.rationale: fp is only a hint; a record with a newer v is listed as needs update.

nodes.label: Service instance name CrossDrop-<8 chars of id>
nodes.rationale: Carries no personal data and rarely clashes; the user's name travels only in TXT n.

nodes.label: PeerList state machine
nodes.rationale: Ignores non-local IPv4 so a hostile advertisement cannot point the app at the internet (hard rule 8).

nodes.label: NetworkMonitor
nodes.rationale: connectivity_plus events plus a 3 s IPv4 poll, debounced 1 s.

nodes.label: iOS LocalNetworkProbe (D-015)
nodes.rationale: bonsoir does not report PolicyDenied, so a Swift probe advertises and browses for itself to detect denial.

nodes.label: MdnsBackend / BonsoirBackend
nodes.rationale: bonsoir (D-012).

nodes.label: IdentityRepository (device UUID and name)
nodes.rationale: drift database (D-013).

nodes.label: UploadClient (streaming upload)
nodes.rationale: Waits for flush() after each 1 MB chunk so at most one chunk sits in the socket buffer.

nodes.label: Sha256Isolate
nodes.rationale: At most 4 chunks in flight so slow hashing slows the transfer instead of using memory.

nodes.label: EphemeralIdentity (per-launch cert, D-011)
nodes.rationale: Phase 1 shortcut: encryption without MITM protection, marked TODO(phase4).

nodes.label: 15 s stall watchdog
nodes.rationale: HttpClientRequest.abort() alone does not unblock a write to a gone peer, so the socket is force-closed.

nodes.label: v1 session and file endpoints (POST sessions, PUT/GET files, complete)
Declared size enforcement
nodes.rationale: Hard rule 6.

nodes.label: Send originals principle
nodes.rationale: Bytes from the library, not re-encoded: HEIC stays HEIC, HEVC stays HEVC (D-039, D-042).

nodes.label: planExport
nodes.rationale: Settings apply only when the receiver is not an iPhone; an unknown receiver counts as Android.

nodes.label: FormatSettings (HEIC to JPEG, Live Photo video)
ExportChannel.swift
nodes.rationale: JPEG at quality 0.92 keeps metadata; HDR gain map is lost.

nodes.label: Receiver save target rules
nodes.rationale: WebM, Matroska, AVI go to Files; anything Photos refuses goes to Files with a note.

nodes.label: Hotspot Configuration capability (D-055)
nodes.rationale: Paid Apple Developer accounts only; default Runner.entitlements omits it so free-account signing (D-017) keeps working; RunnerHotspot.entitlements adds it.

nodes.label: canJoin (reads embedded.mobileprovision)
nodes.rationale: Reads the installed profile so the app reacts to what is really there, even if sideloading strips entitlements.

nodes.label: JoinedHotspot
nodes.rationale: Removes the network CrossDrop added 60 s after the last transfer or 10 min after joining with no transfer.

nodes.label: joinOnce = false
nodes.rationale: A joinOnce network is dropped after 15 s in background or when the device sleeps; CrossDrop pauses and resumes across screen locks, so the network must survive.

nodes.label: Manual join path (Settings > Wi-Fi, Copy password)
tcpReachable check
nodes.rationale: 1.5 s TCP connect detects an iPhone already on the network, avoiding a prompt.

nodes.label: personalHotspotLink (D-057)
nodes.rationale: 172.20.10.0/28 is what iOS uses in practice but is undocumented, so it only drives the hint, never a decision.

nodes.label: peersOnSameNetwork
nodes.rationale: Uses real prefix lengths from the platform; assumes /28 or /24 otherwise.

nodes.label: Three-step Personal Hotspot guide
nodes.rationale: Apps cannot turn on Personal Hotspot; Android joins via the user's own Wi-Fi join rather than WifiNetworkSpecifier.

nodes.label: KeepAliveCoordinator
nodes.rationale: Pure Dart, unit-tested; first begin turns things on, last end turns them off.

nodes.label: KeepAlivePlatform / PlatformKeepAlive
nodes.rationale: Hard rule 9.

nodes.label: Android dataSync foreground service
nodes.rationale: Keeps the process in the foreground with Wi-Fi and wake locks; Android 15 caps dataSync at 6 h/day (D-024).

nodes.label: iOS beginBackgroundTask (20 s budget)
nodes.rationale: iOS suspends background apps; the task finishes the current chunk and saves progress.

nodes.label: Sender pause after current chunk (UploadClient.requestPause)
nodes.rationale: Review M4: a pause asked between uploads or while connecting is kept.

nodes.label: SessionKeepAlive (D-062)
nodes.rationale: Review M3: holds a paused received session 150 s (sender retry deadline plus margin) instead of forever.

nodes.label: GalleryPickerScreen (photo grid)
nodes.rationale: Permissions are asked when the grid opens, never at launch, with mediaLocation (D-037); grid returns only ids/kinds/Live flags, no bytes.

nodes.label: Limited photo access handling
nodes.rationale: iOS Limited and Android 14 selected photos show a banner with Select more and Settings; iOS automatic limited prompt disabled.

nodes.label: Preparer (prepare picks before offer)
nodes.rationale: Runs on Send after the receiver is checked so its platform is known for format rules; iOS exports originals, Android reads in place.

nodes.label: iOS ExportChannel (crossdrop/export)
nodes.rationale: Reads the original resource via PHAssetResourceManager chunk by chunk into staging; 90 s without progress counts as iCloud failure.

nodes.label: Android SourceChannel (crossdrop/source)
nodes.rationale: Opens MediaStore content URIs as descriptors with setRequireOriginal; nothing is copied.

nodes.label: SourceOpener
nodes.rationale: Opens each source once per file and closes it after, so 10,000 files never hold 10,000 descriptors.

nodes.label: Staging folder cleanup
nodes.rationale: Staged batches and SAF grants kept while a send can still resume; orphan batches deleted at launch.

nodes.label: OnboardingGate
nodes.rationale: Shows Home if the database cannot be read rather than locking the user out.

nodes.label: receiveAllowedProvider (D-050)
nodes.rationale: Receiving starts only after onboarding so the iOS Local Network prompt follows the page that explains it.

nodes.label: Just-in-time permission prompts
nodes.rationale: Every permission is asked at the moment it is needed, not on the onboarding pages.

nodes.label: Pinned TLS 1.3 (pinnedHttpClient)
nodes.rationale: Replaces the Phase 1 accept-any-certificate client; wrong certificate fails in the handshake.

nodes.label: Sender authentication by signed challenge
nodes.rationale: dart:io cannot do mutual TLS with unknown certificates (D-027), so the sender proves its key with commit, challenge, sign, token.

nodes.label: crossdrop-commit-v2 commitment (D-061)
nodes.rationale: Binds pinned receiver fingerprint, sender fingerprint and nonce to stop man-in-the-middle relaying.

nodes.label: 6-digit pairing code (derivePairingCode)
nodes.rationale: Shown on both phones for untrusted senders; nonces included in the code (D-029).

nodes.label: Bearer token on /v1/sessions requests
nodes.rationale: Secret inside the pinned TLS stream; never logged or stored; 401 auth_required triggers one re-auth.

nodes.label: Session ownership by sender fingerprint
nodes.rationale: Requests for a session owned by another fingerprint get 404 as if it did not exist.

nodes.label: QR connect payload (crossdrop://connect)
nodes.rationale: Carries ip, port, fp, id, n; unknown params ignored so later hotspot params will not break older apps.

nodes.label: ConnectPayload strict parse
nodes.rationale: Refuses hostile codes: look-alike hosts, non-local IPs, bad escapes; error messages never include the payload.

nodes.label: pickQrAddress (network_monitor)
nodes.rationale: Prefers Wi-Fi client interface, then hotspot, never mobile data or VPN.

nodes.label: Manual IP and port entry
nodes.rationale: No expected id, so any CrossDrop device at the address is accepted; Phase 4 requires the 6-digit code.

nodes.label: Receiver checkpoint (.part fsync then receivedBytes)
nodes.rationale: Every 2 s or 64 MB (D-065); after a crash the part is cut back to the checkpoint since later bytes may not be on disk (D-022); parts live in app support not temp (D-025).

nodes.label: locatePeer (find receiver by device id)
nodes.rationale: After the third failed attempt the sender looks up the receiver by id over mDNS, following a restart on a new random port.

nodes.label: BackgroundFileHash (hashing without re-reading, D-021)
nodes.rationale: Sender hashes in its own isolate in parallel; receiver keeps incremental hash alive across drops so resuming 2 GB does not re-hash 1.5 GB.

nodes.label: saveCollectionFor
nodes.rationale: Chosen from the sanitized name's extension; declared MIME type never used, declared kind only if it matches.

nodes.label: MediaStoreFileStore (Android, crossdrop/save)
nodes.rationale: Writes arriving bytes straight into a pending MediaStore item, so nothing is copied; refused MIME goes to Downloads.

nodes.label: IosPhotosSaver (crossdrop/photos)
nodes.rationale: Moves the verified file into Photos with shouldMoveFile and add-only access asked at Accept (D-043).

nodes.label: Convert HEIC to JPEG / Send Live Photo videos (D-039)
nodes.rationale: Both off by default: originals, still only.

nodes.label: Device name setting (TXT n)
nodes.rationale: At most 63 UTF-8 bytes; rename waits while a transfer is in flight.

nodes.label: lib/app/version.dart
nodes.rationale: A test keeps it equal to pubspec.yaml so no package is needed.

nodes.label: Android ShareChannel (singleTask MainActivity)
nodes.rationale: singleTask so a share reaches the running instance; only other apps' content:// URIs accepted so CrossDrop cannot be made to send its private files.

nodes.label: App Group inbox hand-off (manifest.json)
nodes.rationale: Manifest written last and atomically; inbox taken only after launch cleanup, which keeps staging folders changed in last 10 minutes (review H4).

nodes.label: parseShareManifest
nodes.rationale: Version 1, at most 10,000 items, relative paths inside the share, regular files only.

nodes.label: SendSession (sender queue)
nodes.rationale: The offer is never retried automatically, since a lost reply could leave a duplicate offer.

nodes.label: Accept prompt (60 s timeout)
nodes.rationale: Sender waits 75 s, longer than the receiver's 60 s, and polls GET every 2 s so a broken WebSocket never hides the answer.

nodes.label: Too many bytes fails the file
nodes.rationale: A sender that sends more than declared is broken or hostile; resuming would not help, so that file fails and others continue.

nodes.label: Free space check (offer + open sessions + 64 MB)
SHA-256 verification at complete
nodes.rationale: hash_mismatch with retry restarts from zero once; second mismatch fails the file.

nodes.label: ReceiveHost: Home is the receive screen (D-046)
nodes.rationale: Keeps the receive controller alive above the navigator; server stops 30 s after hidden and idle.

nodes.label: TransferView: one view model for both directions (D-048)
nodes.rationale: ProgressView and ResultView take it as plain widgets so they test without the engine.

nodes.label: Accessibility rules (48 dp, WCAG AA, 2x text)
Files first, then the phone (D-052)
nodes.rationale: Sizes of photos and videos are known only after preparing, so Send shows 'at least' until then.

nodes.label: UsbCameraChannel (crossdrop/usb_camera)
nodes.rationale: Walks folders newest first in pages of 500 so the grid is usable while the rest loads.

nodes.label: buildCameraRoll (Live/edited grouping)
nodes.rationale: Groups by folder and name, strips the E of edited copies; unpaired files become their own tile so no photo is hidden.

nodes.label: ImportRunner (copy queue)
nodes.rationale: Never asks for more bytes than declared, then probes one byte past the end; size_mismatch deletes the item.

nodes.label: PTP over USB via android.mtp.MtpDevice
nodes.rationale: Cable is a direct link and iPhone asks the user to allow access, so no network or TLS; iPhone needs no app (D-067).
